commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Use AITER prebuilt fp8 MoE modules when inter dim is 256 aligned
commits.pr_body:
The modular-kernel harness only pre-shuffles weights (so AITER picks its prebuilt preshuffle_on CK MoE modules) for unquantized and fp8 block schemes. fp8 per-tensor and per-token were excluded entirely because of ROCm/aiter#5766, so every such test JIT-compiles a preshuffle_off module (about 10.5 minutes each in CI). On MI300 this pushes MoE Kernels Shard 1 to about 55 minutes against its 55 minute timeout.

aiter#5766 only rejects intermediate sizes that are not a multiple of 256 (e.g. inter_dim=384). Pre-shuffle fp8 per-tensor/per-token weights too when the intermediate size is a multiple of 256; the 384 padding cases keep JIT-compiling.

On MI300X (rocm/vllm-ci image from amd-ci #14761):
- not multigpu: 48 passed, 6 skipped (same skips as CI); JIT builds drop from 4 kernels (per-tensor/per-token stage 1 and 2) to 2 (stage 2 only).
- multigpu: 27 passed (same as CI).

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Report error type and code like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python's error body is an `ErrorInfo` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/engine/protocol.py`): `type` names the error class and `code` is the HTTP status as an integer. The Rust frontend sends OpenAI-style types (`invalid_request_error`, `server_error`) and string codes (`"model_not_found"`, `"engine_paused"`, `"403"`). A client that switches frontends sees a different `type` for the same failure, and one that reads `code` as an integer, as Python's schema declares it, cannot parse Rust errors. This PR reports Python's class names and integer status codes.

## Claims

Every Rust error response, including streaming `data: {"error": ...}` events, now matches Python's shape:

| Rust error | Status | `type` before → after | `code` before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| invalid request | 400 | `invalid_request_error` → `BadRequestError` | `"invalid_request_error"` → `400` |
| body fails to parse | 400 | `invalid_request_error` → `Bad Request` | `"json_parse_error"` → `400` |
| unknown model | 404 | `invalid_request_error` → `NotFoundError` | `"model_not_found"` → `404` |
| profiler already active | 409 | `conflict_error` → `Conflict` | `"conflict_error"` → `409` |
| internal error | 500 | `server_error` → `InternalServerError` | `"server_error"` → `500` |
| retryable engine rejection | 503 | `service_unavailable_error` → `ServiceUnavailableError` | engine code, e.g. `"engine_paused"` → `503` |
| disabled scale-out route | 403 | `PermissionDeniedError` (unchanged) | `"403"` → `403` |

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2183 tests run: 2183 passed, 13 skipped
```

Batch integration validation on head `c4bb419a8d1c`: formatting, cargo sort, cargo deny, and full workspace Clippy passed. Full nextest ran 2,222 tests: 2,217 passed, 5 failed, and 13 were skipped. The same five failures reproduce on the 14-PR integration tip before this PR; they are model/HF fixture mismatches in unchanged test sources. The required `buildkite/ci/pr` check passed in Buildkite #96193, with 22 jobs passing. Its `:rocket: Upload the picked jobs` step remained blocked, and `docs/readthedocs.org:vllm` was pending when merged.

- `error_response_names_error_class_and_status_code` (`vllm-server`) snapshots the JSON body of every `ApiError` variant.
- Existing route tests now assert the new `type` and integer `code`: unknown model on `/tokenize` and `/detokenize`, malformed JSON, SSE errors after the response started, and the retryable engine rejection on completions, chat, and generate.

## Details

The classes follow `create_error_response` (`serve/exception_handling/error_response.py`). A body that fails to parse into the request model goes through FastAPI's validation handler in Python, which reports the status phrase `Bad Request`, so Rust's `JsonParseError` does the same. Python has no class for 409; like its `HTTPException` handler, `Conflict` uses the status phrase.

The payload is built in one place, `ApiError::to_error_response` (`server/src/error.rs`), and `code` is derived from `status_code()`, so the two cannot disagree. `ErrorDetail.code` becomes a `u16`. `ServiceUnavailable` drops its engine code string: Python surfaces only the engine's message for a retryable rejection (`RetryableRequestError(message)`).

Remaining differences, out of scope here: Python reports `Bad Request` for checks in its pydantic model validators, while the matching Rust DTO `#[validate]` checks report `BadRequestError` (both 400); and Python's LoRA routes use `InvalidUserInput` for bad load/unload input.

Batch integration: vllm-project/vllm#62432 merged before this PR, and vllm-project/vllm#62642 landed earlier in the batch. This PR's `u16` code change needed a one-line update in the 501 route (`code: 501`), recorded in follow-up commit `732b553bd0`.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR changes the Rust error body shape.

AI assistance (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) contributed to the original implementation and the integration adaptation. The human submitter reviewed the original implementation and approved the one-line adaptation in `732b553bd0`.

🤖 Original PR prepared with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code); integration update prepared with OpenAI Codex.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][benchmark][perf] fix moe tuning script for RDNA
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Effective tuning for the fused_moe_triton kernel seems crucial. An optimal .json can results in +15% speedup for GLM4.7-Flash model on gfx1100. However, the existing benchmarking script is very slow (>4hrs with 8 GPUs) due to the large search space, with crashes that hang the ray worker indefinitely. 

This PR addresses three problems for RDNA:

- Remove _matrix_instr_nonkdim_ and _kpack_, which are CDNA only. This reduces the search space up to 4 times as they contribute to name hashings. For some Triton versions, using _matrix_instr_nonkdim_=32 on gfx12 results in "no matching matrix core intrinsic" **HARD FAILURE** for tl.dot. (tensorcore/WMMA is always 16*16*16)
- More pruning based on register spilling - some bad configs even cause low level kernel crashes due to cudagraph hitting illegal memory. so this is necessary.
- Proper Triton cache cleanup for Triton 3.6+

commits.pr_title: [CI][AMD] Deselect distributed tests in the MI300 Model Executor step
commits.pr_body:
## The failure

`(MI300) Model Executor` in [AMD CI nightly 15028](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15028), the only failure among 1282 passing tests:

```
FAILED model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep - RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

The root cause is in the second worker:

```
AssertionError: DP adjusted local rank 1 is out of bounds for 1 devices.
```

## The cause

[#55490](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55490) added `test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep` with `@pytest.mark.distributed(num_gpus=2)` and, in the same commit, added `and (not distributed)` to the pytest command in `.buildkite/test_areas/model_executor.yaml`, for the H200 step and its AMD mirror alike. `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` kept `-m '(not slow_test)'`, and that step runs on `agent_pool: mi300_1`, so a tp=2 test is collected on a single GPU and the second worker has no device to bind.

## The change

The same filter as the upstream step. Collection over `model_executor` goes from 1342 selected and 33 deselected to 1341 and 34; the tp=2 test is the only one removed.

## Tests

The test itself is healthy: with two GPUs visible it passes on MI300 (gfx942, ROCm 10.0), 1 passed in 267.66s. With one GPU visible it reproduces the CI assertion verbatim, and with this change it is deselected instead of collected.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Cap request token histogram buckets at max_model_len
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The five request token-count histograms (`vllm:request_prompt_tokens`, `vllm:request_generation_tokens`, `vllm:request_max_num_generation_tokens`, `vllm:request_params_max_tokens`, `vllm:request_prefill_kv_computed_tokens`) use `build_1_2_5_buckets(max_model_len)` in Python (`PrometheusStatLogger.__init__`, `vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`). The Rust frontend uses a fixed cap of 131072 (with a `TODO` to use `max_model_len`) plus an extra bound at the cap. This PR builds the same bounds as Python from the engine-reported `max_model_len`.

## Claims

- On the Rust frontend, these histograms export Python's bucket bounds for the served model: for `max_model_len=4096`, `1, 2, 5, …, 1000, 2000`.
- Before, every Rust deployment exported `…, 50000, 100000, 131072`: unreachable bounds for short-context models, everything above 131072 in `+Inf` for 1M-context models, and `le` series that do not aggregate with Python's in `histogram_quantile` over a mixed fleet.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2183 tests run: 2183 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `request_token_buckets_are_capped_at_max_model_len` (`vllm-metrics`) renders `vllm:request_prompt_tokens` for `max_model_len=4096` and pins `1.0 … 2000.0 +Inf`. With the old builder's extra bound restored, it fails with an extra `4096.0`.
- The `llm` integration tests (`rust/src/llm/tests/generate.rs`) record these histograms through `Llm`; without the `Llm::new` call they panic on the unset cap, so they cover the wiring.

## Details

The bucket rule stays in `vllm-metrics`, next to the other bucket constants. The global registry is built lazily, before any engine is connected, and a `Family` fixes its metric constructor at registration, so the five families share a small `RequestTokensHistogram` constructor whose buckets are set once through `RequestMetrics::set_max_model_len`. Histograms are created per label set on the first recorded request, which is always after that call. `Llm::new` owns the request metrics and the connected `EngineCoreClient`, so it sets the cap from `client.max_model_len()`: the auto-fitted engine value, the minimum across DP engines, which is also the limit the text layer enforces. The registry is process-global and serves one model, so only the first call takes effect.

Out of scope: `--custom-histogram-buckets` (vllm-project/vllm#48867) can override this family in Python; the Rust frontend rejects the flag at startup (vllm-project/vllm#62431). Supporting it later means filling the same constructor from the override.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR changes these Rust bucket bounds; vllm-project/vllm#58563 adds connector metrics descriptors, not request token buckets.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Return 501 instead of 404 for Python-only routes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Python API server registers several routes for a generate model that the Rust frontend does not serve; under `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` they fall through to axum's default fallback, a bare 404 with an empty body, so clients cannot tell a missing feature from a wrong URL. This PR registers those routes in the Rust router under Python's gating and answers them with an explicit 501 that names the route and points at `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`.

Addresses vllm-project/vllm#55994 (scale-out routes returning 404) without implementing the routes themselves.

## Claims

- `POST /v1/messages`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens`, `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, `/v1/decisions`, `/v1/systemone`, `/scale_elastic_ep`, and `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` return 501 instead of 404.
- The scale-out routes Python registers alongside `/inference/v1/generate` (`/inference/v1/abort_requests`, `/v1/{chat/completions,completions,messages,responses}/render`, `/v1/{chat/completions,completions}/derender`) now follow the same gate as `/inference/v1/generate`: Python's 403 `PermissionDeniedError` stub without `--enable-scale-out`, and 501 with it.
- `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint` is parsed into `ApiServerOptions` (it was accepted as a no-op) and registers `GET /tokenizer_info` with a 501; without the flag the route stays unregistered, as in Python.
- No route the Rust frontend already serves changes behavior.

Example response:

```json
{"error": {"message": "POST /v1/messages is not supported by the Rust frontend yet. Set VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 to use the Python frontend.", "type": "NotImplementedError", "param": null, "code": "501"}}
```

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test` modes), run from the repo root at the branch tip:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                     # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                            # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans  # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2142 tests run: 2142 passed, 13 skipped
```

Each of the six commits also passes workspace clippy (`-D warnings`) on its own.

New route tests in `rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs`:

- `unimplemented_python_routes_return_not_implemented`: each always-registered route returns 501 with the expected message.
- `unimplemented_scale_out_routes_follow_scale_out_gate`: each scale-out route returns 501 with `--enable-scale-out` and 403 without it.
- `tokenizer_info_route_follows_api_server_options`: `/tokenizer_info` returns 501 when enabled and 404 when disabled.

On the base commit (route registrations reverted, these tests kept), `unimplemented_python_routes_return_not_implemented` and `unimplemented_scale_out_routes_follow_scale_out_gate` fail with `404 != 501`.

## Details

Python registration and gating, checked against current `main` ([`launchers/api_server/routers.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/routers.py#L55)):

| Route(s) | Python gate | Rust after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` ([`anthropic/api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py#L51)) | generate task | 501 |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions/batch` ([`chat_completion/api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/api_router.py#L88)) | generate task | 501 |
| `POST /v1/decisions`, `POST /v1/systemone` ([`decisions/api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/openai/decisions/api_router.py#L24), [`structured_decisions/api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/api_router.py#L33)) | always; Python itself answers 501 unless the architecture has a decision strategy | 501 |
| `POST /scale_elastic_ep`, `POST /is_scaling_elastic_ep` ([`elastic_ep/api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/serve/elastic_ep/api_router.py#L28)) | generate task | 501 |
| render, derender, `/inference/v1/abort_requests` ([`scale_out/factories.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/factories.py#L71)) | real handlers under `--enable-scale-out`, 403 stub otherwise | 501 when enabled, the existing 403 stub otherwise |
| `GET /tokenizer_info` ([`tokenize/api_router.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/api_router.py#L87)) | `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint` | 501 when enabled, unregistered otherwise |

The Rust frontend only serves generate models, so the "generate task" gate is always true there.

Ownership and layering:

- Route registration and gating stay in `routes.rs`. The placeholders reuse the existing `ErrorResponse` shape and the existing `disabled_scale_out` stub, and add one `not_supported` handler that reads `MatchedPath` and `Method` to name the route, instead of one handler per route. Each registration carries a `TODO` for the real implementation.
- `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint` follows the `--enable-scale-out` path: parsed in the CLI layer, carried in `ApiServerOptions`, read by the router. It moves out of the no-op args list into `SharedRuntimeArgs`, so the value Python forwards through `--args-json` now reaches the router.

Scope and limitations:

- This only replaces 404s with explicit errors; implementing any of these API families is separate work. Implementing the scale-out render routes on the main router can reuse the standalone `vllm-rs render` handlers, which take `RenderState` rather than `AppState`.
- Not touched, because open PRs implement them: the Responses routes (vllm-project/vllm#58783) and `/generative_scoring` (vllm-project/vllm#46427). Cohere `/cohere/v2/chat` is left out because Python registers it only with `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=1` and the `cohere` SDK installed. FastAPI docs routes (`/openapi.json`, `/docs`, `/redoc`) are not an API contract and are not stubbed.

Not a duplicate: vllm-project/vllm#56124 stubs only the two chat/completions render routes and only when scale-out is enabled (still 404 otherwise); it has had merge conflicts and no activity since 2026-10-07. This PR covers its scope with the gating Python uses. Related open PRs that implement individual families and would replace a placeholder here: vllm-project/vllm#52896 (Anthropic Messages and `count_tokens`, last updated 2026-08-19), vllm-project/vllm#46081 (`/tokenizer_info`, last updated 2026-06-29), vllm-project/vllm#53418 and vllm-project/vllm#53419 (derender, last updated 2026-09-10). vllm-project/vllm#50698 adds an elastic EP control channel but no REST routes.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Emit transfer params at the top level of render output
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since vllm-project/vllm#61241, Python's render routes (`/v1/chat/completions/render`, `/v1/completions/render`) emit `kv_transfer_params` and `ec_transfer_params` only as top-level `GenerateRequest` fields, and `/inference/v1/generate` copies them back into `extra_args`. Rust render still leaves both top-level fields unset and keeps the values inside `sampling_params.vllm_xargs`, so a Rust render followed by a Python generate drops the P/D and E/PD transfer params. This PR makes Rust render hoist them the same way.

## Claims

- Rust render output carries `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` at the top level and no longer inside `sampling_params.vllm_xargs`, matching Python's `_hoist_transfer_params` (`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py`).
- `vllm_xargs` is dropped from the render output when nothing else is left in it, like Python setting `extra_args` to `None`.
- Rust render → Rust generate is unchanged: Rust generate already merges the top-level fields back into `vllm_xargs` (`routes/inference/generate/convert.rs`), and the round-trip test now checks that both params reach the engine request's `extra_args`.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2139 tests run: 2139 passed, 13 skipped
```

`render_chat_response_can_be_submitted_to_generate_unchanged` now sends both transfer params through the render → generate round trip and asserts that they appear at the top level of the render output, that `vllm_xargs` keeps only the unrelated `custom` key, and that both reach the engine request's `extra_args` after generate. With the `render.rs` change reverted, the test fails on the `vllm_xargs` assertion: `{"custom": 1, "ec_transfer_params": {...}, "kv_transfer_params": {...}}` vs `{"custom": 1}`.

## Details

- **Layering.** The render route owns its output wire shape, so the hoist lives in `routes/render.rs` next to `lower_render_request`, mirroring Python's helper. Chat/completions lowering and the shared `merge_*_transfer_params` helpers stay unchanged; generate and the OpenAI routes use them to feed the engine.
- **Non-object values.** A value under `vllm_xargs.kv_transfer_params` that is not a JSON object cannot fit the typed top-level field. It stays where the request put it, which is the current behavior. Python's `vllm_xargs` does not accept object values, so Python never sees this case.
- **Out of scope.** Rust render still emits other xargs under `sampling_params.vllm_xargs`, while Python generate reads `extra_args`; switching that key depends on Rust generate accepting `extra_args` and is left to a follow-up.
- **Duplicate check.** No open PR covers this. Searched open PRs for render/transfer-param and Rust render keywords: vllm-project/vllm#60002 (render token offsets) touches `render.rs` but not the transfer params, and vllm-project/vllm#56814 (reject reserved transfer keys inside `vllm_xargs` at the request merge) is adjacent but does not change the render output shape.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept null for nullable request booleans
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python declares several request booleans as `bool | None`, so an explicit `null` validates and behaves like omission. The Rust frontend declares them as plain `bool` and returns 400 ("invalid type: null, expected a boolean"). This PR accepts `null` for exactly those fields, and resolves the `watermarking` default once in the text layer, as Python's `SamplingParams` does.

## Claims

- `null` now means the same as omission for chat `logprobs`, `stream`, `watermarking`; completions `echo`, `stream`, `watermarking`; generate `stream` and `sampling_params.watermarking`; and `/tokenize` `return_token_strs` (prompt and messages bodies).
- `watermarking: null` keeps watermarking on, as in Python, where `None` requests it.
- Booleans Python declares as plain `bool` (`ignore_eos`, `skip_special_tokens`, `add_special_tokens`, ...) still reject `null` on both frontends.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2186 tests run: 2186 passed, 13 skipped
```

- Chat and completions `nullable_booleans_treat_null_as_omitted`: each field set to `null` deserializes to the same request as omitting it.
- Generate `null_stream_means_non_streaming`, and tokenize `null_return_token_strs_means_false` on both bodies.
- `openai_watermarking_defaults_and_opt_out_reach_engine_core` gains a `null` case: chat and completions, streaming and not, reach the engine with watermarking on.
- Generate `prepare_generate_request_preserves_watermarking_defaults_and_opt_out` gains a `null` case.

All fail on the base.

## Details

Each DTO field's Rust shape follows its Python declaration, so there is one form per case:

| Python declaration | Rust field | `null` |
|---|---|---|
| `T \| None = None` | `Option<T>`; the owner of the `None` meaning resolves it | same as absent |
| `T = d` (not nullable) | `T` with `#[serde(default)]` or `default = "default_true"` | 400, like Python |
| `bool \| None = False` | `bool` with `#[serde(default)]` + `serde_with::DefaultOnNull` | `false` |

`null` handling is a wire-format concern, so it stays on the route-owned DTOs. `watermarking` is `bool | None` on both Python's request and its `SamplingParams`, where `None` means enabled, so it becomes `Option<bool>` through `vllm_text::SamplingParams` and `lower_sampling_params` resolves `None` to `true` in one place. Previously chat, completions and gRPC each resolved it, and generate relied on `SamplingParams::default()` and rejected `null`. `DefaultOnNull` would have turned `watermarking: null` into `false` and silently opted the request out.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR changes `null` handling on these Rust DTOs.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Cap structured-output JSON nesting at 64 levels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python rejects a structured-output JSON schema nested more than 64 levels deep, and a structural tag nested more than 64 + 16 levels, with a 400 (`check_json_nesting` in `vllm/sampling_params.py`, vllm-project/vllm#60036). The Rust frontend has no cap and forwards any schema to EngineCore, where grammar conversion cost grows roughly with size × depth²: vllm-project/vllm#60036 measured 98 s for a depth-512 structural tag. This PR applies the same caps and message in the Rust frontend.

## Claims

- A JSON schema (object or JSON string) nested more than 64 levels, or a structural tag nested more than 80, returns 400 "The JSON schema is nested too deeply: objects and arrays may nest at most 64 levels" before the request reaches EngineCore.
- This covers chat `response_format`, `structured_outputs` on chat, completions, and generate, and the tool-call structural tags that output parsers build.
- A structural tag that is not valid JSON now returns 400 "Invalid structural tag specification." instead of being forwarded to EngineCore, as Python's backend validation does.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2187 tests run: 2187 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `validate_caps_json_schema_nesting` (`vllm-engine-core-client`): 64 levels pass and 65 fail with Python's message, both as a schema object and as a JSON string.
- `validate_caps_structural_tag_nesting_with_wrapper_allowance`: a structural tag passes at 80 levels and fails at 81.
- `validate_rejects_malformed_structural_tag`: a non-JSON structural tag returns "Invalid structural tag specification."
- `prepare_chat_request_rejects_deeply_nested_json_schema` (`vllm-server`): a chat `response_format` with a 65-level schema returns 400 with the message.

The behavioral tests fail with the check removed from `validate`.

## Details

The check lives in `StructuredOutputsParams::validate` (`vllm-engine-core-client`), the existing owner of Python's `_validate_structured_outputs` rules. It already runs at every entry point, including `lower_sampling_params` on the final constraint, so parser-built tool-call structural tags are covered as in Python. A new `nesting` submodule sits next to the existing `xgrammar` one. Every constraint is checked on its parsed value: the schema check runs at the start of `validate_json_schema`, which both JSON branches already call, and a structural tag is parsed and then checked. `serde_json` stops parsing at 128 levels, so a document deeper than that is rejected as invalid JSON (still a 400, with a different message than Python's). For the same reason a structural tag that fails to parse is rejected, so a tag past the parse limit cannot skip the check.

One difference: Rust's parser-built structural tags nest tool argument schemas up to 20 wrapper levels deep (Python's stay within 15), so for that parser a strict tool's parameter schema is effectively capped near 62 levels instead of 64. Real tool schemas are far below either limit, so this PR keeps Python's single 16-level allowance.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR adds a nesting cap to the Rust frontend; vllm-project/vllm#62506 validates JSON Schema keyword values in the Python frontend.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept empty stream_options without streaming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python chat and completions reject `stream_options` without `stream=true` only when the object is non-empty (`if data.get("stream_options") and not data.get("stream")` in each `validate_stream_options`), and `/inference/v1/generate` has no such check. The Rust frontend rejects any `stream_options` with `stream=false` on all three routes, including `{}`. This PR aligns the Rust checks with Python.

## Claims

- Chat and completions accept `"stream_options": {}` without streaming and still reject a `stream_options` object that sets an option.
- Non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` accepts `stream_options`, as in Python; the non-streaming handler already ignores `include_usage` and `continuous_usage_stats`.

| Request with `stream=false` | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|
| chat or completions, `stream_options: {}` | 200 | 400 | 200 |
| chat or completions, `stream_options: {"include_usage": false}` | 400 | 400 | 400 |
| generate, any `stream_options` | 200 | 400 | 200 |

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2186 tests run: 2186 passed, 13 skipped
```

- Chat and completions `validate_request_compat_accepts_empty_stream_options_without_streaming` (`{}`, through both chat layers) fail when the checks go back to `stream_options.is_some()`.
- Chat and completions `validate_request_compat_rejects_stream_options_without_streaming` cover `{"include_usage": false}` and `{"continuous_usage_stats": true}`.
- Generate `validate_request_compat_accepts_stream_options_without_streaming` replaces the test that pinned the rejection.

## Details

`StreamOptions::is_empty` sits on the shared DTO (`routes/openai/utils/types.rs`) and destructures every field, so a new option has to be considered there. Chat has two overlapping checks (the `validate_chat_cross_parameters` schema validator and `validate_request_compat`), and both change together; completions changes `validate_request_compat`. The generate check came from mirroring chat in vllm-project/vllm#43779; Python's generate never had it, so it is removed rather than kept as a Rust-only rejection.

One edge case stays different: Python checks the raw JSON, so it rejects `{"include_usage": null}`; Rust sees the deserialized options and accepts it like `{}`.

Not a duplicate: the only open upstream PR touching `stream_options` and the Rust frontend area, vllm-project/vllm#61275, adds a new Python option and does not change this validation.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Truncate prompts against max_model_len like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python budgets `truncate_prompt_tokens` against the context length only: `-1` keeps `max_model_len - 1` prompt tokens (`TokenizeParams.max_truncation_tokens` in `vllm/renderers/params.py`), and an explicit value is rejected only above `max_model_len`; `max_tokens` is an upper bound clamped after tokenization, not a reservation (vllm-project/vllm#57035, vllm-project/vllm#62010). The Rust frontend budgets `max_model_len - max_tokens` instead. This PR applies Python's budget in the Rust text layer.

## Claims

- `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1` without `max_tokens` now truncates and generates instead of failing as "prompt too long".
- With `max_tokens`, Rust keeps the same prompt tokens Python keeps; generation gets the remaining context through the existing `max_tokens` clamp.
- An explicit `truncate_prompt_tokens` is rejected only above `max_model_len`, with Python's message.

Example with `max_model_len=10`, a 15-token prompt, and `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`:

| `max_tokens` | Rust before | Rust after (= Python) |
|---|---|---|
| absent | 400, prompt too long | 9 prompt tokens, `max_tokens=1` |
| 5 | 5 prompt tokens, `max_tokens=5` | 9 prompt tokens, `max_tokens=1` |

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2183 tests run: 2183 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `auto_truncation_leaves_one_output_token` (`vllm-text`) runs the table above through `TextRequestProcessor::prepare`. It fails on the base: the `max_tokens`-absent case hits the prompt-too-long error.
- `input_budget_holds_back_one_token_for_output` and `fixed_limit_cannot_exceed_max_model_len` replace the unit tests that pinned the old budget.

## Details

Truncation is owned by `vllm-text` (`PromptTruncation::apply`, called from `TextRequestProcessor::prepare_prompt_tokens`), which chat, completions, and gRPC all reach, so one change covers every entry point that accepts `truncate_prompt_tokens`. Only generation paths set a truncation policy (`/tokenize` and `/inference/v1/generate` never do), so the held-back output token always applies, as in Python, where only no-output requests such as pooling keep the full context. `prepare_prompt_tokens` no longer needs `max_tokens`, and the error variant is renamed to `TruncatePromptTokensExceedsMaxModelLen` to match what it checks.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR changes the Rust truncation budget; vllm-project/vllm#61363 changes special-token handling in Python truncation.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept top_logprobs=0 without logprobs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Python chat validator (`check_logprobs` in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`) requires `logprobs=true` only when `top_logprobs` is `-1` or positive, so `top_logprobs: 0` (the OpenAI default) is accepted on its own. The Rust frontend rejects any `top_logprobs` without `logprobs`, so clients and SDKs that always send `top_logprobs: 0` get a 400 that Python would not return. This PR applies Python's condition in the Rust chat checks.

## Claims

- `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `top_logprobs: 0` and no `logprobs` now returns 200 on the Rust frontend, matching Python.
- `top_logprobs: 1` or `-1` without `logprobs` is still rejected with 400.

Without `logprobs`:

| `top_logprobs` | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | 200 | 400 | 200 |
| `1` or `-1` | 400 | 400 | 400 |

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
```

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Validate cache_salt like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python's `validate_cache_salt` (vllm-project/vllm#51444, vllm-project/vllm#54353) rejects a `cache_salt` that is empty, longer than 128 characters, or contains `@`, `/`, `\` or NUL, so unvalidated salts never reach downstream cache backends such as LMCache, which may use those characters as key separators. The Rust frontend only checks a non-empty salt on chat and completions and forwards anything else to the engine; this PR applies Python's rule to every Rust entry point.

## Claims

- `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/inference/v1/generate`, render, and gRPC `Generate` reject a salt that Python rejects, with a 400 (gRPC `InvalidArgument`) instead of forwarding it to the engine.
- Length is counted in Unicode code points, matching Python's `len`.
- Valid salts and omitted salts behave as before.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repository root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2140 tests run: 2140 passed, 13 skipped
```

New test `vllm-text` `request::tests::validate_rejects_unsafe_cache_salt` covers a valid salt, a salt of exactly 128 code points (`é`, two bytes each), the empty string, 129 characters, and each forbidden character. With the check in `TextRequest::validate` removed, the test fails.

## Details

- **Where the check lives.** `TextRequest::validate` is the shared chokepoint that every Rust entry point calls before tokenization (`TextLlm::prepare`, `tokenize`, `tokenize_in_place`), and it already holds similar request invariants such as `EmptyStopString`. Putting the rule there covers HTTP and gRPC with one check. The new `Error::InvalidCacheSalt` is a request-validation error, so it maps to a 400 through the existing `text_submit_error` and `chat_submit_error`. The DTO-level `#[validate(length(min = 1))]` checks on chat and completions are kept; they only give an earlier message for the empty case.
- **Error message.** Python raises two messages (empty vs. length/charset); Rust uses one message that states the whole rule.
- **Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#56681 (open, no activity since 2026-09-21) targets the same Rust gap but checks at lowering time (`lower_text_request`), which runs after tokenization, and also adds an engine-side check in `vllm/v1/request.py`. This PR is Rust-only and validates before tokenization at the shared chokepoint; the engine-side check is out of scope. No other open PR touches Rust `cache_salt` validation.
- **AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and the test results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Inherit presence and frequency penalties from generation_config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since vllm-project/vllm#50769, the Python frontend takes `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty` from the model's `generation_config.json` as server-side sampling defaults. The Rust frontend still ignores them, so a model that ships `"presence_penalty": 1.5` samples with `0.0` when the request omits the field. This PR makes the Rust frontend inherit both penalties the same way it already inherits the other generation-config defaults.

## Claims

- `generation_config.json` `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty` now become defaults for Chat Completions and Completions requests that omit them, matching Python's priority order (request value → server default → OpenAI default `0.0`).
- `--generation-config vllm` still ignores model-provided defaults, including the two penalties.
- Explicit request values still take precedence over the model defaults.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repository root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2139 tests run: 2139 passed, 13 skipped
```

Changed tests in `vllm-text`:

- `lower_sampling_params_uses_generation_defaults_when_user_omits_values` now expects `presence_penalty: 1.5` and `frequency_penalty: 0.5` from the defaults. It fails when the production change in `lower.rs` is reverted.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Clamp logit_bias to [-100, 100]
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python's `SamplingParams.from_optional` clamps every `logit_bias` value to `[-100, 100]` for every entry point, so a bias of `250` behaves like `100`. The Rust frontend forwards the value to the engine unchanged, so the same request samples differently on the two frontends. This PR clamps biases in `vllm_text::lower_sampling_params`.

Supersedes the inactive draft vllm-project/vllm#50350, which clamps in the HTTP-only `convert_logit_bias` helper.

## Claims

- Rust clamps each `logit_bias` value to `[-100, 100]` before it reaches engine-core, matching `SamplingParams.from_optional`.
- The clamp applies to every Rust entry point: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/inference/v1/generate`, and gRPC.
- In-range values are unchanged; key parsing and the out-of-vocab check are unchanged.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test` modes), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2140 tests run: 2140 passed, 13 skipped
```

New test: `vllm-text` `lower_sampling_params_clamps_logit_bias` (`{5: 250, 6: -300, 7: 1.5}` lowers to `{5: 100, 6: -100, 7: 1.5}`). With the fix reverted and the test kept, it fails: `left: Some({6: -300.0, 5: 250.0, 7: 1.5})`.

## Details

- **Where the clamp lives.** `vllm_text::lower_sampling_params` turns northbound sampling params into engine-core params, and every Rust entry point goes through it. Python clamps at the equivalent point, `SamplingParams` construction. Clamping in `convert_logit_bias` (as in vllm-project/vllm#50350) would miss `/inference/v1/generate` and gRPC, which do not use that helper.
- **NaN.** `f32::clamp` keeps NaN, while Python's `min(100.0, max(-100.0, nan))` returns `-100.0`. Over HTTP this cannot happen, since `serde_json` rejects a body with a `NaN` literal; over gRPC a NaN float would pass through unclamped. This PR leaves NaN alone: the open draft vllm-project/vllm#62038 proposes rejecting NaN biases in Python instead, and Rust should follow whichever behavior lands there.
- **Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for `logit_bias` (`clamp`, `Rust`, title-only). vllm-project/vllm#50350 is the only open PR for this item: a draft with no activity since 2026-09-24 that clamps in the HTTP-only helper. vllm-project/vllm#62038 (Python NaN rejection) and vllm-project/vllm#60562 (V2 sampler caps) touch different behavior.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Reject silently dropped request fields on chat, completions, and generate
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Python frontend honors several request fields on chat, completions, and `/inference/v1/generate` that the Rust frontend silently drops: chat and tokenize ignore unknown keys through serde defaults, and completions and generate collect them into an unused catch-all map. A client that sets one of these fields today gets a 200 with output that ignores it. This PR declares each field on the Rust DTO and returns an explicit 400 for non-default values, while absent, `null`, and Python's default value still pass, so requests from SDKs that send defaults are unaffected. It also fixes two trivial gaps: `length_penalty: 1.0` is accepted, and generate's `sampling_params.extra_args` reaches the engine.

## Claims

- Chat and completions return 400 for `return_weight_versions: true`; chat returns 400 for `return_prompt_text: true`; completions returns 400 for any `prompt_embeds` (Python also rejects it unless `--enable-prompt-embeds`, which the Rust frontend does not support).
- `/inference/v1/generate` returns 400 for `output_mode: "text"`, for non-empty `sampling_params.stop` or `include_stop_str_in_output: true`, and for any `sampling_params.trace_decode_token_ids`. `output_mode` is typed as an enum mirroring Python's `OutputMode`, and `stop` reuses the `StringOrArray` type chat and completions use, so malformed values fail deserialization as in Python.
- Chat and completions accept `length_penalty: 1.0` (Python's default), which previously got a 400; other values are still rejected.
- `/inference/v1/generate` accepts `sampling_params.extra_args` (Python's `SamplingParams` field name) as an alias of `vllm_xargs`, so it reaches the engine instead of being dropped.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test` modes), run from the repository root at the branch tip:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2149 tests run: 2149 passed, 13 skipped
```

Each commit also passes workspace clippy (`-D warnings`) on its own.

Every item has a unit test pinning the contract: the default/absent/`null` values pass and the non-default value is rejected, or, for `extra_args`, the value reaches the lowered request's `vllm_xargs` alongside the merged `kv_transfer_params`. With the fix reverted locally, `prepare_generate_request_accepts_python_extra_args` (no alias) and the chat `validate_request_compat_rejects_only_non_default_length_penalty` (no default filter) fail as expected.

## Details

Field-by-field Python anchors (all checked on current `main`):

| Route | Field | Python default | Python consumer | Rust behavior after this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chat, completions | `length_penalty` | `1.0` | beam search only | accept `1.0`; 400 otherwise (unchanged) |
| chat | `return_prompt_text` | `None` | adds `prompt_text` to the response | 400 when `true` |
| chat, completions | `return_weight_versions` | `false` | adds per-choice `weight_versions` spans | 400 when `true` |
| completions | `prompt_embeds` | `None` | renderer; 400 unless `--enable-prompt-embeds` | 400 when present |
| generate | `output_mode` | `"tokens"` | `"text"` returns detokenized text and decoded logprobs | 400 for `"text"` |
| generate | `sampling_params.stop`, `include_stop_str_in_output` | `None`, `false` | detokenizer stop matching | 400 for non-empty `stop` or `true` |
| generate | `sampling_params.trace_decode_token_ids` | `None` | engine trace replay; 400 unless `--enable-trace-replay` | 400 when present |
| generate | `sampling_params.extra_args` | `None` | engine `extra_args` | serde alias of `vllm_xargs` |

Ownership and layering:

- Protocol fields belong to the server DTOs, so every check sits at the HTTP boundary in each route's existing `validate_request_compat`, before lowering, using `bail_invalid_request!`.
- Generate sampling fields that the shared `vllm_text::SamplingParams` does not model are declared on the existing `GenerateSamplingParams` wrapper, next to `n`, which exists to reject such keys explicitly instead of dropping them.
- `extra_args` is a `#[serde(alias)]` on `vllm_text::SamplingParams::vllm_xargs`. That type is flattened into the generate DTO and already owns the field; lowering and transfer-param merging are unchanged.

Limitations and follow-ups:

- `stop` / `include_stop_str_in_output` and `output_mode: "text"` on the generate route are rejected until the route detokenizes. Both need the same text-layer detokenizer on the token-only route and are left as a follow-up; vllm-project/vllm#51904 (open, no activity since 2026-09-29) implements stop strings there and would replace this placeholder.
- `return_weight_versions` is a placeholder only. The spans already reach the engine output, and `/inference/v1/generate` already returns them; wiring them through chat and completions (including stop-string truncation) is a separate change.
- `length_penalty` only matters for beam search, which the Rust frontend does not implement; vllm-project/vllm#47705 (open, no activity since 2026-08-05) adds beam search and replaces this check.

Behavior change: requests that set these fields to non-default values used to get a 200 with the field ignored and now get a 400. The most likely case is P/D pipelines that render with the Python frontend and generate with the Rust frontend while forwarding client stop strings: generation used to run past the stop, and now fails explicitly. Python render's empty `stop: []` and `include_stop_str_in_output: false` still pass.

Not a duplicate: open PR searches for each field found no PR adding these checks. The related open PRs are vllm-project/vllm#51904 and vllm-project/vllm#47705 above, which implement the features behind two of the placeholders, and vllm-project/vllm#56814, which touches `vllm_xargs` reserved keys and is orthogonal to the `extra_args` alias.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR; the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --trust-request-chat-template
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python refuses a request that brings its own chat template unless the server runs with `--trust-request-chat-template` (`OnlineRenderer.validate_chat_template`, `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`), with a 400: "Chat template is passed with request, but --trust-request-chat-template is not set. Refused request with untrusted chat template." The Rust frontend rejects the flag at startup and its HF renderer compiles and renders any request `chat_template`, so a request can run an arbitrary Jinja template on a server whose operator never opted in. This PR supports the flag and refuses untrusted request templates where the Rust frontend compiles them.

## Claims

- `--trust-request-chat-template` is accepted by `vllm serve` with the Rust frontend (through `--args-json`), `vllm-rs serve`, and `vllm-rs render`.
- Without the flag, a request `chat_template` on chat completions, `/tokenize`, or the render route returns 400 with Python's message; with it, the template is rendered as before.
- `/tokenize` now maps request validation errors from chat preparation to 400 instead of 500, as chat completions already does, so this refusal and other request errors there (for example a template's `raise_exception`) are client errors, as in Python.

| Request `chat_template` | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|
| set, flag off | 400 | rendered | 400 |
| set, flag on | rendered | startup fails on the flag | rendered |

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2185 tests run: 2185 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `chat_template_refuses_untrusted_request_override` (`vllm-chat`): an untrusted HF renderer refuses a request template with a request validation error and still renders requests without one. It fails with the check removed. The existing override tests now run with a trusted renderer.
- `untrusted_request_chat_template_maps_to_invalid_request` (`vllm-server`): the error maps to 400 with Python's message through `chat_submit_error`, which `/tokenize` now uses.
- `frontend_config_trusts_request_chat_template_from_args_json` (`vllm-cmd`): the flag in `--args-json` reaches the server config.

## Details

The check sits where a request template is consumed: `HfChatRenderer::apply_chat_template`, the only place that compiles one. The renderer receives the flag once at load through `LoadModelBackendsOptions`, next to the server-default `chat_template`. The flag moves from the unsupported-argument list to the shared runtime arguments (and the `render` arguments).

Differences from Python, documented on the flag and on `ChatOptions.chat_template`:
- Only the HF renderer honors a request template. The native renderers (DeepSeek, Harmony, and the other model encoders) ignore it whether or not it is trusted, while Python refuses an untrusted one for every renderer except Harmony.
- A `chat_template` key inside `chat_template_kwargs` is not refused: Rust passes it to the template as an ordinary variable and never compiles it, while Python treats it as a template override.
- `--no-trust-request-chat-template` is not accepted, like the other inverse boolean spellings on the Rust CLI.

Not a duplicate: no open upstream PR implements this flag for the Rust frontend; vllm-project/vllm#62374 (configurable template fuel) leaves a TODO for request templates once this flag lands.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Make unhandled `vllm serve` frontend flags explicit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python `vllm serve` reads `--custom-histogram-buckets`, `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, and `--enable-elastic-ep` in the frontend, but the Rust frontend did not declare them and dropped them without a warning. This PR makes them fail startup (`Unsupported`). It also accepts `--disable-fastapi-docs` as a no-op, since Rust serves no API docs routes.

## Claims

- `--custom-histogram-buckets`, `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, and `--enable-elastic-ep` now fail startup on both `vllm-rs serve` and the Python-supervised `--args-json` path, instead of being silently ignored by the frontend.
- `--disable-fastapi-docs` is accepted with a no-op warning instead of failing startup. The Rust frontend serves no OpenAPI, Swagger, or ReDoc endpoints, so it already behaves as if the flag were set.

## Validation

Rust CI commands (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`, `style-clippy` and `test` modes), run from the repository root at the branch tip:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2142 tests run: 2142 passed, 13 skipped
```

These ran before the structured-outputs commit was reverted; after the revert, `cargo nextest run -p vllm-cmd` (82 passed) and `cargo clippy -p vllm-cmd --all-targets` are clean.

Each commit also passes workspace clippy with `-D warnings` on its own.

New tests in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/tests.rs`:

- `unsupported_args_fail_startup`: each of the three flags fails `vllm-rs serve` parsing and is listed in the `--args-json` startup error.
- `noop_args_are_accepted`: `--disable-fastapi-docs` parses on both paths.

With `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs` reverted to `main`, both new tests fail.

## Details

**Where the code lives.** Argument recognition belongs to the CLI layer. The flags reuse the existing `Unsupported` / `Noop` markers in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs`, which already apply to both the `vllm-rs serve` (clap) and `--args-json` (serde) paths. No new mechanism is added.

**Why each flag is rejected rather than ignored.**

- `--custom-histogram-buckets` replaces the default buckets of the frontend Prometheus histograms ([`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py#L821)). The Rust histograms use fixed buckets, so the requested buckets were silently not applied.
- With `--enable-tower-connector-lora`, Python's `InputProcessor` prefixes the multimodal hash with the LoRA name so encoder-cache entries do not collide across adapters ([`vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py#L297-L311)). Rust always sends the bare hash, so with the flag on, the engine could reuse encoder outputs computed under a different adapter.
- With `--enable-elastic-ep`, Python's core client hands engine input sockets over during scaling ([`vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/852989f580820849113d67d13fd8053e279d0444/vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py#L637)) and the API server exposes the scaling routes. The Rust frontend has neither, so it could not follow a scale event that the engine went through.

**`--structured-outputs-config`.** An earlier revision forwarded it to the managed engine. vllm-project/vllm#62456 parses it in the Rust frontend (it selects the structured-outputs backend) and forwards it itself, so this PR reverts that part and leaves the flag untouched.

**Behavior changes for existing users.**

- `--disable-fastapi-docs` now starts instead of failing.
- The three new `Unsupported` flags were either not honored by the Rust frontend before or could produce wrong results with it.

**Not a duplicate.** Searching open PRs for each flag finds no PR that changes how the Rust frontend handles them. vllm-project/vllm#50698 (inactive since 2026-10-02) adds a supervisor-side control channel for elastic EP scaling but does not touch `--enable-elastic-ep` handling in the Rust CLI. vllm-project/vllm#50101 edits the neighboring `stream_interval` entry in `unsupported.rs`, a different flag.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Ignore token stream intervals for pooling
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Prevent pooling requests from crashing AsyncLLM's output handler when `--stream-interval` is greater than one.

## Claims

- Skip token-stream buffering for pooling completion and cancellation.
- Keep generation's existing stream-interval behavior.

## Validation

On main at `68ebea7`, pooling completion and cancellation with stream intervals greater than one raise the missing-detokenizer `AssertionError`. The same cases pass on this branch. The output-processor suite and scoped pre-commit hooks pass.

To run the related suites in a configured development environment:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine
```

The [requested GPU serving check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55226#issuecomment-5613201182) used Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B on an RTX 5070 Ti with MRV2, `--runner pooling`, and `--stream-interval 2`. Sequential and batched embedding requests returned HTTP 200, and the server remained healthy. That serving check was run in September and has not been repeated.

## Details

Pooling requests have no detokenizer. Return their results before token buffering so pooling and generation handling stay separate.

This overlaps #56131, which uses a detokenizer check for the same failure. Maintainers should choose one implementation.

commits.pr_title: [CI][AMD] Shard the MI300 V1 Spec Decode step
commits.pr_body:
# [CI][AMD] Shard the MI300 V1 Spec Decode step

## The failure

`:amd: (MI300) V1 Spec Decode` timed out in AMD CI nightly [15028](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15028) after 50m57s against a 50 minute limit. Nothing failed: the job was killed with 467 of 494 tests done, in the middle of `test_speculators_eagle3.py::test_eagle3_speculators_model[llama3-eagle3-speculator]`.

## The problem

The step runs the whole suite in one job and has been growing for weeks:

| build | date | selected | duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14162 | 7 Oct | 377 | 27:30 |
| 14707 | 15 Oct | 378 | 31:45 |
| 14810 | 16 Oct | 386 | 33:28 |
| 14934 | 19 Oct | 494 | 38:43 |
| 15028 | 20 Oct | 494 | killed at 50:57 |

14934 and 15028 ran an identical set of 494 tests, so the last 12 minutes did not come from new tests. Weight loading did: 686 s over 39 loads in 14934 against 1513 s over 37 loads in 15028, which is half of the job's wall time. Cold reads sustain only 16-19 MB/s per stream on these agents, and because `_prefetch_checkpoint` reads each file with one sequential loop, a 4-shard checkpoint can only use 4 of the 8 prefetch threads. The two jobs also ran on different nodes, `gpu90e3` and `gpu8e72`, with different amounts of pre-existing page cache.

Two things rule out the suite itself. The same command on `:amd: (MI355 DPX) V1 Spec Decode` finishes in 23.9, 24.0 and 24.3 minutes in the same three builds. And compute is not growing: torch.compile accounts for 80 s of the 51 minutes, and AITER does no JIT compilation at all, it imports the prebuilt `module_aiter_core.so`.

## The change

Shard the step across two jobs with the `--shard-id` / `--num-shards` pattern already used by the other 30 sharded MI300 and MI355 steps in this file. The upstream mirror for this step in `.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` sets `automatic_shard: true`, which upstream CI resolves to two shards; `test-amd.yaml` has no equivalent key, which is why this one step kept absorbing the growth.

Two is what the same step already runs as upstream, where the shards finish in 23.2 and 18.1 minutes in `vllm/ci` 95866, and 16.0 and 15.3 minutes in 96000. Each shard still pays the cold checkpoint reads for the models it touches, so this is not a clean halving; upstream 96100 shows one shard at 38.7 minutes on a slow node, which is the same storage effect described above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Build Pixtral vision position ids on device
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes the `Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` CI job, where `test_pixtral.py::test_chat_consolidated` fails on main in every full build (e.g. [95829](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95829), [95887](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95887)) with `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected`.

## Claims

- The Pixtral vision encoders no longer do a blocking host-to-device copy on every encoder forward: both the Mistral-format `VisionTransformer` and the HF-format `PixtralHFVisionModel` (used by Mistral3) on transformers >= 5.17.
- `test_chat_consolidated` passes again under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, and the HF-format path no longer trips the check either. Outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

On 1x GB300 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and transformers 5.20.2 (the CI pin):

| Path | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Mistral format: `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_pixtral.py -k test_chat_consolidated` | failed, `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `pixtral.py:1033` (same trace as CI) | 1 passed, logprobs match the stored H100 reference |
| HF format: `mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512` loaded from `model.safetensors` (`Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`), one image chat request | failed, `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `pixtral.py:1596` | passes; greedy output identical to main run with the sync check disabled |

## Details

`position_meshgrid` built the per-patch `(row, col)` coordinates with `torch.arange` on the CPU, and `VisionTransformer.forward` then moved them to the GPU with `.to(self.device)`. The source tensor is pageable, so the copy blocks the host, which the sync checker in CI (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`) reports as a failure. The fix creates the coordinates directly on the device of the patch embeddings, which removes the copy.

The HF-format path (`PixtralHFVisionModel`) has the same pattern in `position_ids_in_meshgrid`. It is fixed the same way. CI does not catch it today because the HF-format Pixtral tests are skipped as large-GPU tests. Its `.to(self.device)` stays, because on transformers < 5.17 the function delegates to the transformers implementation, which still builds the ids on the CPU. When the ids are already on the device, the call does nothing.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo-V2: skip fused fp8 qkv_proj tensors for layers the model does not have
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip fused fp8 `qkv_proj` checkpoint tensors for decoder layers the `MiMoV2Model` instance does not have, as every other branch of `load_weights` already does. Related: #58142 (same loader, pending-pair state across calls).

## Claims

- A checkpoint with more decoder layers than the instance, e.g. `--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": N}'`, no longer fails engine init with `AttributeError: ModuleList has no attribute 'N'` in `_try_load_fp8_qkv_proj`.
- One regression test through `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` guards this fix and #58142.

## Validation

`tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py::test_load_weights_pairs_split_fp8_qkv_proj_and_skips_absent_layers` builds a one-layer `MiMoV2Model` and calls `load_weights` twice. The present layer's `weight` / `weight_scale_inv` pair is split across the calls, and an absent layer's pair arrives within the first. The test asserts the returned loaded set, the dequantized values of the loaded layer against the unquantized source (existing helpers in the file), and an empty `_pending_fp8_qkv_proj`.

```
pytest tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py -q
```

CPU only (macOS arm64, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0, `uv` venv with this tree on `PYTHONPATH`):

| `mimo_v2.py` | result |
|---|---|
| `main` (`cc9b0f097d`) | 1 failed, 19 passed: `AttributeError: ModuleList has no attribute '7'` |
| this PR with #58142's persistent pending dict reverted | 1 failed, 19 passed: the split pair is dropped |
| this PR | 20 passed |

`pre-commit run --files` (ruff, mypy, typos) clean on both changed files. CI runs this file in the Quantized Models step.

End to end, on an earlier head with the same fix (`a1538ff185`): `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL` with `--hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers":16}'` loads and serves on one GB300. Output is garbage, as expected for a truncated model, but it boots.

Model evaluation: not applicable. The new branch only runs for a checkpoint tensor with no matching parameter, which a full-depth model never has (pipeline-parallel missing layers are caught earlier by `is_pp_missing_parameter`), so the weights loaded for full models are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes this path. #46755 adds fused fp8 `qkv_proj` loading to the MTP loader (`mimo_v2_mtp.py`), not `MiMoV2Model.load_weights`.

## Details

`_try_load_fp8_qkv_proj` buffers a layer's fused `qkv_proj` weight and scale until both arrive, then calls `self.get_submodule(<layer>.self_attn)`. For a layer the instance does not have, that raises. Since #58142 made the pending dict persist across `load_weights` calls, a lone absent-layer tensor would otherwise also stay pending for the model's lifetime. The fix returns early when `<prefix>.weight` is not in `params_dict`, matching the expert and generic branches. Truncated boots take minutes instead of hours, which is what makes bisection on this model family practical (context: #58142, https://al-engr.com/gb300-mimo-v26-pro-testing.html).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the regression test, run the checks above, and draft this description.

commits.pr_title: [MyPy][4/N] Fix mypy errors in medium-hard tests/ dirs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

PR 4 of #49569, covering the "medium-hard" test directories. Fixes every mypy error in them at the stricter `follow_imports=silent` setting and routes them into `SILENT_GROUPS` in `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, so the fixes are enforced. Claimed [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49569#issuecomment-5552556980).

**511 errors → 0** on current `main` (`10f6ab01a`):

| Directory | Errors on `main` | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tests/v1/kv_offload` | 232 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/worker` | 94 | 0 |
| `tests/parser` | 64 | 0 |
| `tests/model_executor` (incl. `model_loader`, `kernels`) | 49 | 0 |
| `tests/renderers` | 28 | 0 |
| `tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text` | 20 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/metrics` | 13 | 0 |
| `tests/v1/streaming_input` | 11 | 0 |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` | 0 | 0 |

With #51043 merged, `tests/model_executor` is a single silent-group entry, and this PR no longer touches `tests/model_executor/layers`.

## Approach (reworked per review)

- **No `cast()` anywhere.** Fixes use, in order:
  1. Runtime-true narrowing (`assert x is not None`, `assert isinstance(...)`, small typed narrowing helpers, e.g. for `EMABackpressureDetector` in `test_backpressure.py`).
  2. Stubs fixed once per file (`MockVllmConfig`, stand-in builders with honest return types).
  3. `MagicMock(spec=...)`, only where it can't make a test vacuous.
  4. A scoped `# type: ignore[code]` with a reason.

  `cast(X, None)`, `cast(Any, ...)` and `_NO_BACKEND` are gone. `supports_eagle3` uses `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)`.
- **Ignores.** Monkeypatched methods use `monkeypatch.setattr`, as PR 3 did. That includes the 4 older `method-assign` ignores that were already in these dirs on `main`, so there are 0 left. The 36 remaining scoped ignores (12 `type-abstract`, 7 `list-item`, 6 `misc`, 3 `call-arg`, 3 `attr-defined`, 2 `override`, 2 `dict-item`, 1 `call-overload`) each carry a reason. Starting fresh from `main` with `--warn-unused-ignores`, the migrated directories had 8 unused ignores; they now have 0. The two `apply_post_tokenization` ignores were already unused on `main` before the overloads below went in, so the overloads didn't remove them. The overloads are kept because they give callers the precise return type.
- **`vllm/` fixes folded in:**
  - `RayPrometheusMetric.labels() -> Self` (the 7 casts in `test_ray_metrics.py` disappear and that file is unchanged from `main`).
  - `@overload`s on `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization`.
  - `"azacinto_foscolo"` in `AudioAssetName`.
  - `StreamingInput.prompt: PromptType | EngineInput`, because its consumers, `process_inputs` and `extract_prompt_components`, already take `PromptType | EngineInput`.
- **HiSparse.** No cast and no issue: production always passes a `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup`, and the base class only appears because the test registers without a HiSparse config.

## Defects the type checker surfaced

1. **`RoutingMethodType.FUSED_TOPK` doesn't exist** (`tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`). Any read of `DummyRouter.routing_method_type` raised `AttributeError`, and `FusedMoE` does read that property. Fixed to `TopK`.
2. **Dead setup writes in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`.** `worker.refines_row_mirrors` and `worker._layer_mirror_callbacks` exist nowhere in `vllm/`, left behind by an upstream refactor. `test_hisparse_appends_reference_slots_within_a_mirror_phase` reads as if it toggles a row-mirror mode, but that setup did nothing. Removed.
3. **Dead observer attributes in `test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py`.** `slot_mapping_observer` and `host_mirror_forward_observer` likewise exist nowhere in `vllm/`. Removed.
4. **`CPUExpertsFp8` → `CPUExpertsInt4`.** The old test built its "monolithic" expert from a non-monolithic class, so it never reached the replay-support check. #59455 has since fixed this independently on `main`, so it's no longer in this diff.
5. **Wrong helper annotation in `test_obj_tier.py`.** `lookup_and_wait` was annotated `-> list[bool]` but returns `list[LookupResult]` (matches `test_fs_tier.py` now).
6. **Missing isinstance check in `test_factory.py`.** It lacked the `assert isinstance(spec, CPUOffloadingSpec)` its siblings have.
7. **`DUMMY_TOOLS` raw dicts (found, not changed here).** In `tests/parser/engine/replay_harness.py`, raw dicts are assigned to `request.tools`, and pydantic never validates them (no `validate_assignment`). The tool-schema helpers skip non-`ChatCompletionToolsParam` entries, so the parsers see no tool schema. Since fixing it changes what runs, it's left out of this PR; happy to send it separately.

## Behaviour changes

**None.** The three changes you flagged (`DUMMY_TOOLS`, `mock_request`, `block_ids`) are reverted. Every change is now a type annotation, a runtime-true assert, an equivalent rewiring, the `FUSED_TOPK` fix, or removal of writes to attributes nothing reads.

## Annotation issues in `vllm/` worked around (follow-up candidates)

- **`GDNAttentionBackend`** doesn't implement the abstract `get_impl_cls`, so mypy treats it as abstract, which causes the `type-abstract` ignores in the worker tests. Model classes that subclass protocol interfaces with optional members are treated as abstract for the same reason.
- **`EMABackpressureDetector.default_config`** is annotated `-> dict | None` but always returns a dict.
- **`VllmJitKernel.dispatch(self, **kwargs: Any)`** makes subclasses with named keyword-only parameters fail the override check.
- **`supports_eagle3` / `supports_eagle` overloads** list `type[object]` first. With `nn.Module` resolving to `Any`, a model *instance* matches the class overload, and `TypeIs` narrows it to `type[SupportsEagle3]`. That's why `test_plamo3.py` and `test_qwen3_omni.py` use `assert isinstance(target, SupportsEagle3)` (the helper's exact body) instead of calling the helper.

## Test Plan

```bash
# strict-group mypy on every target file + changed vllm/ files, all CI Python versions
mypy --python-version {3.10,3.11,3.12,3.13} <target dirs> vllm/{assets/audio,engine/protocol,renderers/params,v1/metrics/ray_wrappers}.py
mypy --python-version 3.10 --warn-unused-ignores <target dirs>
ruff check / ruff format --check (v0.14.0) and typos on all changed files
python -c "from tools.pre_commit.mypy import group_files; ..."   # routing
# CPU (macOS, torch 2.13, VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty):
pytest tests/parser tests/renderers
pytest <every changed test file outside parser/renderers>
```

## Test Result

- **mypy:** `Success: no issues found in 254 source files` with `--warn-unused-ignores` on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13; 0 `cast` added.
- **ruff / format / typos:** clean. All changed test and `vllm/` files route to the strict default group.
- **`tests/parser` + `tests/renderers` (CPU):** 6,814 passed, 3 failed. The 3 failures are in `test_hf.py` and need gated Hugging Face models (Llama-3.2 / PaliGemma return 401). They fail identically on `main`.
- **Other changed test files (CPU):** 936 passed, 132 skipped, 89 failed, 1 collection error. I re-ran the exact same tests on `main`'s test files in the same environment, and the failure set is identical: 0 fail only on this branch. They need CUDA or compiled ops (`kv_offload/cpu` transfers, Triton launchers) or extra packages (`datasets`).

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for the type cleanup, this review rework and verification. The submitter is responsible for every changed line and for defending the contribution before merge.

commits.pr_title: [CI][LoRA] Release punica test GPU memory before later engine tests
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) LoRA Shard 1/2` on main. It failed deterministically on builds 96078, 96080 and 96081, on three different hosts:

```
ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (21.55/32.5 GiB) on startup is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.85, 27.62 GiB).
FAILED lora/test_qwenvl.py::test_qwen2vl_lora - RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

**Root cause:** `tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py` overrides the autouse `cleanup_fixture` with a no-op (#47534) to keep its ~4400 kernel tests fast. So `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` never runs, and the pytest process keeps about 11 GiB of cached GPU memory after the module finishes. Engines started earlier in the same job saw ~31.9 GiB free; after the punica tests, `test_qwenvl` sees 21.5 GiB.

This was harmless until LoRA moved to runtime auto-sharding (#62084). The planner then went from 3 shards to 2 and put `test_punica_ops.py` and `test_qwenvl.py` in the same shard; files run alphabetically, so punica always comes first:
- 96065 (passed): `shard 1/3 runs 97 tests in 8 files`, no punica.
- 96078 (failed): `shard 1/2 runs 4522 tests in 9 files`, with punica before qwenvl.

No code in `vllm/lora`, `tests/lora` or `.buildkite` changed between the passing and failing builds.

**Fix:** keep the per-test override, but add a module-scoped autouse fixture that calls `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` once after the module. The punica tests keep their speedup, and later engine tests in the same process get the memory back.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches `test_punica_ops.py` or this failure.

## Test Plan

Not run locally (no GPU here). The LoRA steps' CI will confirm.

## Notes

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed by the submitter.
