commits.pr_title: [Perf] Enable PDL for fused MoE top-k gating
commits.pr_body:
## Overview The FP32 router GEMM supports programmatic dependent launch (PDL), but fused MoE `topkGating` uses an ordinary launch. Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+ with CUDA 12+, allowing it to start early and wait before reading producer-dependent data. ## Claims - On GB200, the M=4 MiniMax-M3 router-to-gating CUDA Graph chain saves **0.486 us (-9.12%)** with hot weights and **0.466 us (-7.77%)** with rotating weights. - In ordinary MiniMax-M3 aggregated serving, mean TPOT improves **0.61–1.16%** at request concurrency 1/16/32. All three paired runs improve for both tested input lengths at these concurrencies. C4 is effectively unchanged. - Pure-prefill C16/C32 mean TTFT regresses **0.54%/0.49%**. The results support a modest decode benefit on this setup; broader workload and platform coverage remains open. ## Validation **End-to-end accuracy (`713192bab`):** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, concurrency 8), MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, TP8 on the same 8x GB200 GPUs, with real EAGLE3 verification and three draft tokens. Each variant ran twice without restarting its server. | Strict-match accuracy | Baseline | PDL | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Run 1 | 1247/1319 (94.54%) | 1248/1319 (94.62%) | | Run 2 | 1254/1319 (95.07%) | 1249/1319 (94.69%) | | Mean | 94.81% | 94.66% | Mean change is -0.152 percentage points; baseline repeats differ by 0.531 points. These two repeats per variant do not establish accuracy equivalence. All evaluation requests succeeded. Baseline uses official vLLM v0.29.0; the candidate overlays the pinned PR kernel in the same image, rather than a full PR checkout build. **Serving:** MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, 8x GB200 on two four-GPU nodes, TP8 with expert parallelism disabled, one aggregated worker, FP8 KV/indexer cache, FlashInfer/TRTLLM attention, no prefix caching or speculative decoding. Direct `vllm serve` / `vllm bench serve` uses the same physical GPUs for A/B, three valid pairs per workload, and 64 measured requests per variant per pair. | Request concurrency | TPOT change, ISL/OSL 128/1024 | TPOT change, 8192/1024 | TTFT change, 8192/1 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | -0.61% | -0.63% | +0.89% | | 4 | +0.05% | -0.01% | -0.12% | | 16 | -1.16% | -1.00% | +0.54% | | 32 | -0.93% | -1.09% | +0.49% | Negative latency changes are better. Changes are computed within each pair and then averaged. For 128/1024 C1, mean TPOT is 3.874 → 3.851 ms; individual paired changes range from -0.82% to -0.48%. These finite bursts and three repeats do not establish statistical significance or sustained-load capacity. **Kernel chain:** M=4, H=6144, E=128, top-4 sigmoid; three same-GPU A/B pairs. Hot-weight latency is 5.330 → 4.844 us. Rotating weights use 64 distinct 3 MiB matrices; paired changes range from -8.28% to -6.51%. Each repetition ends with a non-PDL serial boundary to prevent overlap into the next repetition and premature logits-buffer reuse. Its approximately 0.682 us cost is included equally. Latencies are medians across rounds; savings are medians of paired differences. Isolated gating with that boundary saves 0.076 us (-2.16%). **Correctness and integration:** - 866 unchanged upstream fused-top-k and FP32-router tests passed against the pinned runtime with the PDL overlay. - 360 representative original-versus-patched operator cases per process match with zero tolerance: FP32/FP16/BF16, expert counts 6–512, selected index types/top-k values, bias, normalization, padding, ties and nonfinite values. Equal NaNs are accepted; NaN payload-bit identity is not asserted. - 1,200 preallocated-chain and 960 runtime-dispatch changing-input graph checks passed, including poisoned intermediates and the M=32/33 dispatch boundary. - The changed SM100a CUDA translation unit compiled; the original standalone harness passed Compute Sanitizer memcheck with zero errors. - All 74 raw serving measurements completed: 4,736 requests, zero failures. One JIT-contaminated pair is excluded and replaced as described below. - Separate untimed GPU traces confirm PDL gating on all eight TP ranks. Directly adjacent router/gating calls overlap in residence in 6,720/6,720 patched pairs versus 0/6,720 baseline pairs. Residence includes dependency waits; it does not directly measure time saved.
Runtime pins, commands and measurement controls The serving, kernel-chain and correctness/integration results above use vLLM `9ea8f3ffc354901b740f0b31988900897b7221d7`, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and CUDA 13.0. Those measurements used the PR CUDA file on base `d2125ea681784c17251c47939f5ed6d1c67384f8`, before the later guard simplifications. Both controls load identically recompiled original/patched translation units, with library hashes verified on every TP rank. This is not a full current-main rebuild. The upstream tests were copied unchanged from the PR base into that pinned runtime. Equivalent in-checkout commands: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py -v ``` Example client command; sweep the listed length pairs and C=1/4/16/32: ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \ --model nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 64 --num-warmups 8 \ --ignore-eos --seed 1729 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --metric-percentiles 50,90,95,99 --save-result --save-detailed ``` Server limits: model length 16384, batched tokens 16384, sequences 32, CUDA Graph capture limit 64, block size 128 and GPU memory utilization 0.9. FlashInfer autotuning and `float32_matmul_precision=high` are enabled. Each variant starts fresh workers and autotuning. Paired variants use the same seed and workload order; the main sequence is A/B, B/A, A/B. Round 0 used eight warmups and exposed attention JIT during measured 8192/1024 C32 requests. That whole pair is excluded. Later pairs use `max(8, 2*C)` warmups; a dedicated same-GPU A/B with verbose JIT monitoring replaces the excluded pair. Neither replacement measurement has observed measured-window JIT. Raw excluded results are retained; each workload has three valid pairs. Capture, JIT/warmup, correctness checks and diagnostic traces are outside timing. Request-level P99 has only 64 samples per run and is descriptive. Eager host-wall results are retained separately from graph GPU timings. The microbench and overlay harnesses are external to this 30-line CUDA diff. ## Details The dependency wait and completion signal precede dependent reads and row-dependent exits. CUDA launches set the PDL attribute without a host architecture query, matching `topk_softplus_sqrt` and `per_token_group_quant`, and check `cudaLaunchKernelEx` errors. Device-side PDL instructions remain guarded by `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900`. Routing math, launch geometry, output layout and the operator API are unchanged. ROCm and the unfused fallback retain their existing paths. Hopper, ROCm and a full current-main build remain unvalidated. For the host-launch cleanup in `09647c0364`, `git diff --check` and `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu` passed. GPU tests were not rerun for this cleanup; the accuracy results above remain pinned to `713192bab`. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation and this description. ## Summary

Part of #54966 (item 1): `AiterExperts` already declares production support for the GFX950-only MXFP4 W4A16 (`kMxfp4Static, None`) and W4A4 (`kMxfp4Static, kMxfp4Dynamic`) quant schemes, but neither was exercised through the modular-kernel (`tests/kernels/moe`) prepare/finalize -> fused-experts -> reference-compare test harness. This PR adds that coverage.

- Adds a `weight_dtype` field to `TestMoEQuantConfig`/`Config` (mirrors `FusedMoEQuantConfig.make()`'s own `(quant_dtype, weight_dtype)` split) to represent the asymmetric W4A16 case (mxfp4 weight, unquantized activation) alongside the symmetric W4A4 case.
- Reuses the production MXFP4 oracle directly instead of reimplementing weight-layout conversion: `convert_gpt_oss_weight_to_mxfp4_moe_kernel_format()` and `make_mxfp4_moe_quant_config()` from `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py`.
- Moves `_interleave_gate_up_rows()` out of `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` into the shared `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py` helper module.

Three gaps were found while validating on MI350/gfx950 hardware and are scoped around rather than fixed here:
- W4A16's heuristic-dispatch kernel only has a `SWIGLUOAI` specialization, not SILU/GELU, despite `AiterExperts._supports_activation()` declaring broader support (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2419).
- W4A16 hits the same `topk=1` + `apply_router_weight_on_input` GPU-hang gap as AITER's existing block-scaled FP8 path (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2418), just not representable via `config.quant_block_shape` since mxfp4 has no block-shape field.
- W4A16+`SWIGLUOAI` silently computes the wrong thing for bias-free SwiGLU-OAI (~55% sign agreement, ~5x-small magnitude on hardware) instead of raising; only smoke-tested (shape/finite) here until the fix in #59766 lands.

## Test plan

Validated on an MI350/gfx950 host (MXFP4 is unsupported on MI300/gfx942):
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py::test_modular_kernel_combinations_singlegpu -k mxfp4` — both new W4A16 and W4A4 cases pass (note: `AiterExperts` was split into per-scheme subclasses in #60322, so the original `-k "AiterExperts and mxfp4"` filter no longer matches any test id; use `-k mxfp4`)

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k mxfp4` — existing W4A16 unit tests still pass after moving `_interleave_gate_up_rows`

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Test] Stop requesting capfd in the subprocess weight cache test
commits.pr_body:
## The failure

`(MI300) Model Executor` in [AMD CI 14934](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14934), the only failure among 1238 passing tests:

```
FAILED model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep - TypeError: cannot pickle '_Local' object
```

## The cause

[#55490](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55490) added `test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep`, which combines `@create_new_process_for_each_test()` with the `capfd` fixture. The wrapper cloudpickles its arguments into the child process and `CaptureFixture` holds a thread-local, so the test raises before it runs. It is the only test in the file with that combination, and the failure is deterministic: the pickle happens before any GPU work.

## The change

The test no longer requests `capfd`. `DSV2_EP_CASE` leaves `check_flashinfer_cache` off and every use of `capfd` in `run_cold_start_and_warm_restart` sits behind that flag, so the fixture was requested but never read. It could not have worked in the child either, which inherits the parent's descriptors. The helper keeps it as an optional parameter, so the in-process cases retain their autotune-cache assertions.

A wider fix, dropping unpicklable fixtures inside the wrapper in `tests/utils.py`, would silently change behaviour for other tests, so this stays local to the one test that is wrong.

## Tests

`test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep` fails on `main` with the error above and passes with this change: 1 passed in 216.64s on MI300 (gfx942, ROCm 10.0) with 2 GPUs, through baseline, cold start, daemon, warm and restart.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

FIX #62466

`histogram_2048_topk` in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` can return indices `>= seq_len`. This happens when the row length is not a multiple of 4 and the top-k threshold lands in the fp16 `-inf` bin. This PR skips lanes past `seq_len` in the collection loop and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- `persistent_topk` no longer returns indices past the row length on the `histogram_2048_topk` path (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows).
- The out-of-bounds reads of `logits` in the refinement pass are gone.
- Rows with length % 4 == 0 and rows whose threshold is above the `-inf` bin are unchanged. The guard only drops lanes that were never real elements.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130. `_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt from this branch; main measured with the precompiled wheel for 3e96f9cf6.

New test, `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail`. It covers k in {512, 1024, 2048}, length = k + {1, 2, 3, 4}, 0 or 100 finite scores, and in-row fill of `-inf` or `-1e30`:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k masked_row_tail
main:     36 failed, 12 passed   (every length % 4 != 0 case fails; % 4 == 0 passes)
this PR:  48 passed
```

Sample failure on main: `AssertionError: row 0: indices outside [0, 513): [513, 514, 515]`.

Op-level repro (1 row, k = 512, stride 516, every in-row score `-inf`, padding 0.0):

```text
            main                      this PR
len=513:    [513, 514, 515]           []
len=514:    [514, 515]                []
len=515:    [515]                     []
len=516:    []                        []
```

compute-sanitizer memcheck, one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`:

```text
main:     3 x "Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes" in histogram_2048_topk<512>, kernel aborts
this PR:  ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```

Full file with this PR: `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` gives 294 passed, 44 skipped (platform-gated cases).

No end-to-end serving repro: no shipped model reaches this path (see Details). CI runs this test file on Blackwell (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause. The last float4 load of a row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. They are binned like real elements. The collection loop gates candidates only on `vec_valid = i < n_vec`. When fewer than k in-row scores are above the `-inf` bin, the threshold is that bin, so the tail lanes become "equal" candidates. Refinement then reads `logits[idx]` for them and can output them.

Fix. Add `in_range = vec_valid && elem_idx < seq_len` and use it for `is_above` and `is_equal`. Tail lanes still count in the histogram, but that does not move the threshold. They only add to the `-inf` bin, the lowest non-NaN bin, so the counts above it are unchanged. And since `seq_len > k`, the in-row elements alone already reach k at the `-inf` bin.

Reachability, and why there is no end-to-end repro. The kernel path needs a decode row with k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows, and the persistent backend. The persistent backend is picked by `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, by `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, or by `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. The bug also needs fewer than k in-row scores above the fp16 `-inf` bin. I checked every in-tree caller:

- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 style DSA decode (`sparse_attn_indexer`): in-row scores come from `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` and are finite. Prefill uses `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not this kernel.
- Qwen4-exp QSA: scores are sums of ReLU terms, so they are finite and >= 0.
- Step5 rejects the persistent backend.
- DeepSeek V4.1 `apply_candidate_mask` does write `-inf` inside decode rows. But the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 tokens (16384 positions) on full-length (`compress_ratio` 1) layers. Every row on this path (<= 8192) is therefore fully covered.

So no shipped model reaches the bug with default or near-default flags. Reaching it needs a config with `candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size < index_topk`, or more than `length - k` scores at or below about -65504. The layer-level script in the issue shows the V4.1 composition (`apply_candidate_mask` then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`) with such a candidate set. If the bug were hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so the result would be wrong KV slots with no error.

`cooperative_topk`, `histogram_256_topk` and the radix path are not affected. I checked lengths 8193 to 70001 with all-`-inf` rows on main and saw no bad indices.

Performance: one extra compare per element in the collection loop. No measurable change expected; not benchmarked.

---

commits.pr_title: [Pooling] Improve SPLADE throughput 3.6% to 7.8%
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR speeds up SPLADE max pooling by batching the `dense/GELU/layer-norm` transform and applying `relu/log1p` after max reduction. Vocabulary projection still runs per sequence, and dense embeddings, classification, sum pooling, and the full MLM-head forward remains as is.

## Output on main / on branch

`naver/splade-cocondenser-ensembledistil`, BF16, **L32 / HTTP concurrency 1**, four fresh-server pairs. B is sequences per HTTP request; values are means and paired 95% intervals.

| GPU / B | Inputs/s main → branch | HTTP req/s | Gain [95% CI] | HTTP p50 ms | HTTP p99 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 / 16 | 401.76 → 424.44 | 25.11 → 26.53 | +5.65% [+5.14, +6.15] | 32.14 → 29.97 | 34.51 → 32.11 |
| H100 / 32 | 433.69 → 466.42 | 13.55 → 14.58 | +7.54% [+4.60, +10.55] | 55.69 → 51.38 | 58.99 → 53.58 |
| H100 / 64 | 556.74 → 599.92 | 8.70 → 9.37 | +7.76% [+6.71, +8.82] | 88.52 → 80.14 | 91.11 → 81.57 |
| B300 / 16 | 726.79 → 756.97 | 45.42 → 47.31 | +4.15% [+3.12, +5.20] | 19.23 → 18.37 | 21.26 → 20.20 |
| B300 / 32 | 829.05 → 858.84 | 25.91 → 26.84 | +3.59% [+2.11, +5.09] | 32.47 → 31.22 | 34.46 → 33.16 |
| B300 / 64 | 997.59 → 1034.75 | 15.59 → 16.17 | +3.72% [+3.29, +4.16] | 53.15 → 50.73 | 55.74 → 53.26 |

Full SciFact, 5,183 documents / 300 queries, raw sparse embeddings without L2 normalization:

| Reference | nDCG@10 | Recall@100 |
|---|---:|---:|
| H100 main BF16 | 0.709244 | 0.948667 |
| H100 branch BF16 | 0.709244 | 0.948667 |
| B300 main BF16 | 0.708963 | 0.948667 |
| B300 branch BF16 | 0.708963 | 0.948667 |
| HF FLOAT32 | 0.707913 | 0.948667 |
| HF BFLOAT16 | 0.708922 | 0.948667 |

**Accuracy result:** No retrieval-quality regression was observed on SciFact. On both H100 and B300, the branch preserved main’s nDCG@10, Recall@100 and every query’s top-10 result ordering. Scores were comparable to the HF FP32/BF16 references; the raw-vector norm and numerical-error checks are reported below. This conclusion covers the tested checkpoint and SciFact dataset; the later merge from `main` has not been re-evaluated.

nDCG@10 measures how well relevant documents rank in the top 10; Recall@100 measures how many relevant documents appear in the top 100 (higher is better for both). Using raw embeddings without L2 normalization preserves their magnitudes, so normalization cannot hide changes in vector scale.


## Test Plan

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_splade_sparse_pooler.py -x -q` — **12 passed**; pre-commit passed. Separate parity checks passed on CPU, H100 and B300 (48 cases each). API accuracy and mixed C1/C16 checks ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`; same-hidden-state comparisons ran separately. **No new CI cost; no tests or files added.**

<details>
<summary>Memory, numerical results and measurement limits</summary>

Three fresh servers per variant, after warmup; allocated/reserved/NVML process peaks are distinct metrics (MiB):

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|

Isolated B64/L32 pooler peak allocation increased 11.20 → 12.34 MiB; B64/L128 fell 33.50 → 30.59 MiB on both GPUs. These are separate metrics.

Worst numerical errors across all SciFact vectors, branch versus reference:

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

This is a custom BEIR-style evaluation, not an official MTEB run: title + text, right truncation at 512, raw sparse dot products, stable ID ties and same-ID exclusion. Dataset pins: `BeIR/scifact@b3b5335604bf5ee3c4447671af975ea25143d4f5`, qrels `2938d17dc3b09882fdb8c12bbbe2e2dc0e75a029`. H100 HF references were retained from the same frozen environment; B300 references were rerun. Mixed-batch encoder outputs vary on main too; this is reported separately from pooler parity, not treated as proof of a race.

Secondary serving results (four pairs):

| GPU / workload | Inputs/s main → branch | Change [95% CI] | HTTP p50 ms | HTTP p99 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 / B8/L128/C8 | 995.22 → 989.84 | -0.54% [-1.83, +0.76] | 62.81 → 63.09 | 65.85 → 66.25 |
| H100 / B64/L128/C8 | 998.04 → 1002.87 | +0.48% [-0.30, +1.27] | 499.08 → 496.02 | 514.38 → 510.65 |
| B300 / B8/L32/C1 | 574.10 → 592.54 | +3.21% [+2.01, +4.43] | 12.08 → 11.67 | 14.95 → 14.41 |
| B300 / B8/L128/C8 | 1097.30 → 1098.48 | +0.11% [-0.40, +0.62] | 56.85 → 56.80 | 64.39 → 64.34 |
| B300 / B64/L128/C8 | 1286.15 → 1296.82 | +0.83% [+0.36, +1.31] | 387.25 → 384.05 | 414.62 → 410.38 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Parse multi-line JSON arguments in the DeepSeek V3 and V3.1 parsers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60342. The `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31` tool parsers lose tool calls whose JSON arguments the model pretty-prints over several lines: their regexes match the arguments with `.`, which stops at a newline.

## Claims

- Tool calls with multi-line JSON arguments are now parsed by `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31`, in both streaming and non-streaming mode.
- Single-line arguments and parallel tool calls are unchanged.

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue, run through the test helpers with the real tokenizers (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1`), with `{"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}` dumped with `indent=2`:

| Parser | Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | non-streaming | no tool calls (`tools_called=True`, `tool_calls=[]`) | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v3` | streaming | `get_weather` with arguments `{` | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v31` | non-streaming | no tool calls | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v31` | streaming | `get_weather` with arguments `{` | `get_weather` with the full arguments |

Added `test_multiline_json_arguments` (DeepSeek-V3, two parallel calls with pretty-printed arguments) and `test_extract_tool_calls_with_multiline_arguments` (DeepSeek-V3.1), each run in streaming and non-streaming mode. All four cases fail on main and pass with this change.

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py
22 passed, 1 xfailed
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` pass on the changed files.

These ran on CPU (WSL, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`, with the post-test GPU cleanup skipped since there is no accelerator). I did not run a server end to end with a DeepSeek-V3 checkpoint, which needs a multi-GPU node; the change is limited to the parsers' regexes.

## Details

- Root cause: `DeepSeekV3ToolParser` matches `function_arguments` with `.*` (`` .*[^\n`] `` when streaming), and `DeepSeekV31ToolParser` with `.*?` / `.*`. Without `re.DOTALL`, `.` doesn't match `\n`, so the non-streaming regex finds nothing and the streaming regex captures only the first line of the arguments.
- Fix: only the arguments group uses `[\s\S]`. It stays non-greedy in the regexes used with `findall`, so parallel calls still split at the first closing tag. The type and function-name groups keep `.`, so a name can't span lines and the whole pattern doesn't need `re.DOTALL`.
- The Rust frontend's parsers (`rust/src/parser/src/tool/deepseek_json`) don't use a regex here; `take_json_object` scans the object by brace depth, so from reading the code they already handle pretty-printed arguments. Only the Python parsers change.
- Related PRs: #60361 (opened a few minutes before this one, still a draft) makes the same change to the V3 regexes and leaves V3.1 for later; this PR covers both parsers. #47503 edits the same DeepSeek-V3 regexes to accept an optional newline before the JSON fence, which is a different case, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase. #55473 wraps these regexes with timeouts and is independent.

AI assistance was used for this change (tracking down the cause, writing the tests and this description). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
